_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 35 (Beth-El return; Rachel's death; Reuben's transgression; Isaac's death). Saadia-specific: v.2 'מעבודאת אלג'רבא' = 'foreign worshipped-objects' (concrete substitute for אלהי הנכר); v.7 'אלטאיק' = 'the Power' (= Beth-El's God); v.8 מרג אלבכא = 'Allon-Bachut' rendered as 'plain of weeping'; v.13 'נור אללה' = 'light of God' (consistent anti-anthropomorphic); v.18 'אבן תרחי' = 'son of my deathly anguish' for בן אוני; v.22 'אמה' אביה' = 'his father's maidservant' (not 'concubine' — softening).

translations.1: Then God said to Jacob: 'Arise, go up to Beth-El, and stay there; and make there an altar to the Power who appeared to you when you fled from before Esau your brother.'
translations.2: And Jacob said to his household and to all who were with him: 'Remove the foreign worshipped-objects which are among you, and purify yourselves, and change your garments.
translations.3: And let us arise and go up to Beth-El; and let us make there an altar to the Power who answers me in the day of my distress, and who has been with me in the way which I have walked.'
translations.4: And they gave to Jacob all the foreign worshipped-objects which they had with them, and the earrings which were in their ears; and he buried them under the terebinth which is over against Nablus (Shechem).
translations.5: Then they journeyed; and the dread of God was upon the dwellers of the towns which were around them; and they did not pursue the sons of Jacob.
translations.6: And Jacob came to Luz which is in the land of Canaan — that is Beth-El — he and all the people who were with him.
translations.7: And he built there an altar; and he called the place Beth-El to the Power — for there had God revealed Himself to him in his flight from before his brother.
translations.8: And Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, died; and she was buried below Beth-El, beneath the plain; and he named it the Plain of Weeping.
translations.9: And God appeared to Jacob again, on his coming from Paddan-Aram; and He blessed him.
translations.10: And He said to him: 'Your name is Jacob; your name shall not be called Jacob alone any more, but Israel.' And He named him also Israel.
translations.11: Then God said to him: 'I am the Sufficient Power; grow and multiply. A nation and a host of nations shall be from you; and kings shall come forth from your loins.
translations.12: And the land which I gave to Abraham and Isaac — to you shall I give it; and to your offspring after you.'
translations.13: Then the light of God ascended from him, at the place where He had addressed him.
translations.14: And Jacob set up a pillar at the place where He had addressed him — a pillar of stone; and he poured upon it a drink-offering, and poured upon it oil.
translations.15: And Jacob named that place where God had addressed him — Beth-El.
translations.16: Then they journeyed from Beth-El; and there was still a mile's distance of the way for them to come to Ephrath, when Rachel bore — and her bearing was hard.
translations.17: And when her bearing was hard, the midwife said to her: 'Fear not, for this too is a son for you.'
translations.18: And as her soul was going out — for she was dying — she named him Son-of-My-Deathly-Anguish (Ben-Oni); but his father named him Benjamin.
translations.19: And Rachel died, and was buried on the way to Ephrath — that is Bethlehem.
translations.20: And Jacob set up a pillar upon her grave; that is the Pillar of Rachel's grave to this day.
translations.21: Then Israel journeyed on, and pitched his tent from there to Migdal-Eder.
translations.22: And when Israel dwelt in that land, Reuben went and lay with Bilhah, his father's maidservant; and Israel knew of it. And the sons of Jacob — with Benjamin — were twelve:
translations.23: Sons of Leah: Reuben the firstborn of Jacob; and Simeon, and Levi, and Judah; and Issachar, and Zebulun.
translations.24: Sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.
translations.25: And the sons of Bilhah, Rachel's maidservant: Dan and Naphtali.
translations.26: And the sons of Zilpah, Leah's maidservant: Gad and Asher. These are the sons of Jacob who were born to him in Paddan-Aram.
translations.27: Then Jacob came to Isaac his father, to Mamre, to Kiriath-Arba — that is Hebron — where Abraham and Isaac had dwelt.
translations.28: And the lifetime of Isaac was a hundred and eighty years.
translations.29: And he expired and died, and was gathered to his people — an old man satisfied with years; and Esau and Jacob his sons buried him.
